key_insight: CFD Forge combines an LLM-driven agent with deterministic, physics-based checks so the model can automate CFD workflows while fixed criteria decide whether results are accepted.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce manual effort in meshing, solver setup, debugging, and reporting for repeated CFD studies, making high-throughput design and active-learning loops more practical.
method: LLM interprets the engineering request and selects actions from a closed set for case construction, meshing, solver execution, diagnostics, and reporting.
Flow-specific deterministic acceptance checks evaluate explicit criteria and override model judgment when deciding whether a run is acceptable.
Validated on a converging-diverging nozzle, a 2D forward-facing step, and a turbulent cube retrospective test with recorded simulation states.
evidence_signal: In replay tests over 36 recorded simulation states, the model accepted 12 of 13 detectable faults when judging without check outputs, but accepted none when CFD Forge’s deterministic checks controlled the decision.
watch_item: Reliance on predefined check rules means coverage depends on how well each flow type’s acceptance criteria are designed and registered.
paper_title: CFD Forge: A Physics-Constrained Agentic Framework for Autonomous CFD
